selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: Who is the main figure mentioned in this passage, and what mission is he on?
questions.answer: He is a traveler sent into the world to reach faith, and he is searching for his Creator with certainty.

questions.question: How did this traveler carry out his search before this new stage began?
questions.answer: He examined the whole universe in his mind and asked created things about their Maker.

questions.question: What had he already reached with full conviction before starting this new journey?
questions.answer: He had reached certainty that his Creator necessarily exists.

questions.question: What did the traveler say to his intellect at the start of the new journey?
questions.answer: He invited his intellect to join him in a fresh journey to observe proofs that Allah is One.

questions.question: What is the main subject of this chapter?
questions.answer: It is about evidences for Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: At the first stopping-place, how many major truths did they see?
questions.answer: They saw four sacred truths.

questions.question: What was special about those four truths in relation to the whole universe?
questions.answer: They were seen as ruling over the entire cosmos.

questions.question: What did they discover at the first stop of the journey?
questions.answer: They found four holy truths spread across the universe.

questions.question: What made those truths important?
questions.answer: They clearly demanded the conclusion that Allah is One.

questions.question: What title is given to this section of the work?
questions.answer: It is a chapter about proofs of Divine unity.

questions.question: Why had the traveler been sent to the world, according to the passage?
questions.answer: He had been sent to gain faith.

questions.question: What does the traveler look for in every place?
questions.answer: He looks for his Lord and seeks to find Allah everywhere through the signs of creation.

questions.question: What does the phrase about traveling through the whole cosmos “in his mind” show?
questions.answer: It shows that his journey is mainly one of thought, reflection, and understanding.

questions.question: What certainty had the traveler already achieved?
questions.answer: He had become certain of the existence of his Creator.

questions.question: What was the purpose of beginning a new journey after reaching that certainty?
questions.answer: It was to see the evidences that prove the Creator is absolutely One.

questions.question: Who joined the traveler in this new stage?
questions.answer: His intellect joined him.

questions.question: What relationship between belief in Allah’s existence and belief in His unity is implied here?
questions.answer: It implies that after recognizing Allah exists, a person should go on to recognize that He is One without partner.

questions.question: What kind of person is the traveler presented as being?
questions.answer: He is presented as a sincere seeker trying to reach true faith.

questions.question: What name is used for the Creator in a way that highlights certainty of existence?
questions.answer: The Creator is described as the Necessarily Existent One.

questions.question: After reaching certainty about existence, what issue becomes the focus of the next journey?
questions.answer: The next focus is proving Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: Why is it meaningful that the traveler speaks to his intellect?
questions.answer: It shows that reason has an important role in understanding faith.

questions.question: What happened when the traveler and his intellect set out together?
questions.answer: They arrived at the first stopping-place and witnessed four sacred truths across the cosmos.

questions.question: What does the passage say those truths do by themselves?
questions.answer: It says they plainly require belief in Allah’s unity.

questions.question: Does the passage describe these truths as local and limited, or universal and wide-reaching?
questions.answer: It describes them as universal and spread over the whole cosmos.
